info.name: BPCC List Management API v3.2
info.description:
Overview

Bright Pattern's List Management API supports a wide range of functionalities previously only accessible within the Contact Center Administrator application. Version 3.2 delivers expanded list and campaign management functionality, introducing comprehensive API support for Do Not Call (DNC) lists and improved methods for accessing Calling List records.

Bright Pattern's List Management API 3.2 enables you to:

  • Manage outbound campaigns, including their DNC list (new*) and calling list associations

  • Update outbound campaign states, access their information, and view their results

  • Create new lists and new formats

  • View and update (new*) calling list properties

  • Manage calling list and DNC list records individually or in bulk

  • Retrieve the contents of Calling Lists not associated with campaigns (new*)

  • Create, retrieve, update, and delete DNC lists (new*)

Note: To ensure compatibility with the last API version and facilitate seamless migration, all previously available methods are retained as is. However, methods with a "DEPRECIATED" tag in their name are not recommended for usage and have new corresponding methods defined for their respective functionalities.

This document describes the available REST API methods, specifies their functionality, and provides example requests and responses. Individual methods, as well as the entire List Management API 3.1 collection, can be loaded into Postman and interacted with via your unique Bright Pattern Contact Center access token.

new* - added since List API 3.0

item.name: Authentication

request.description:
This method returns an access token that will be used to authenticate each subsequent request made via this API.

Note: Access Tokens expire after 1 hour and require renewal.

Supplementing invalid credentials in any of the parameters will return a 401 Authentification failed response. Client authentification will also fail if the selected user is locked out or disabled, or the chosen tenant is inactive.

Note: Clients are authenticated using OAuth 2.0 Client Credentials Grant, therefore, thegrant_type parameter is always set to 'client_credentials'. Examples of other parameter values can be found in the Request body below.

item.description:
The authentification method described in this section is the first step required to successfully use Bright Pattern's List Management API. The clients of this API are authenticated in correspondence with the OAuth 2.0 Client Credentials Grant. Requests made via this API are authenticated via an access token.

Note: Only the users with corresponding privileges can perform selected operations via this API. The complete list of privileges can be found here.

To obtain the access token:

  1. Login to the Contact Center Administrator application.
  2. Navigate to the Users page. Select or create a user with privileges corresponding to the tasks you wish to perform via the List Management API.
  3. Click the Generate button to generate an API secret. Copy the generated key and note the username for the next steps.
  4. Use the Get Access Token method to obtain an access token. Set the client_id to the username and client_secret to the generated API secret key.
  5. Use the value of access_token, returned in the response, to set the Authorization: Bearer [access token] headers of each subsequent request made via the List Management API.

request.description:
This method returns all campaign settings. To request only specific parts of the settings (e.g., only assigned teams), use the include query parameter with comma-separated values. If include is not specified, the method behaves the same as Get Campaign 3.1 (backward compatible). Possible values for include are:

  • \\*: Returns all settings

  • generalSettings

  • callerIdSettings

  • outboundGeneral

  • teams

  • callerIDs

  • dispositions

  • lists

  • dncLists

Note: The include query parameter is not supported for Outbound Messaging campaigns.

request.description:
This method removes the instance of a list from the associated campaign. The instance to be removed is specified by its unique identifier, instanceID, returned in the response body of the Get Campaign method (see here).

Note: Bright Pattern Contact Center solution supports several voice campaign modes (see here). Depending on the mode of the associated campaign, the active call behavior will differentiate as follows:

  • Progressive, Predictive, or Automatic (IVR) campaigns
    • Upon instance deletion, all active, i.e. in a dialing state, within a script, or connected to an agent, calls are dropped
  • Preview campaigns
    • Upon instance deletion, only the calls not yet picked up by an agent are dropped. In-progress and connected calls are not affected

The results of completed calls are archived and available for downloading in the Contact Center Administrator application (see here). Interaction results for dropped calls are not saved.

request.description:
This method returns a copy of an existing record in an instance, as well as the information about the last interaction associated with this record. The instance is specified by its unique identifier, instanceID, returned in the response body of the Get Campaign method (see here). The search for the record is performed based on the defined key fields.

Before the record is queried, its existence in the specified list is checked. If the record does exist in the specified list, the record is queried successfully.

Note: If a PHONE type field is defined as a key, the record value is checked for a full match with the value stored in the database or the original source (if the data was modified upon loading into the database).

Note: The response body contains the List Record JSON Object, defined by two sub-objects as follows:

  • entry object: contains a copy of the list entry
    • field names are retained as defined at list creation
      • custom fields are returned with the prefix 'custom_' added to the name defined in the Administrator Application
    • time and date field values are returned in UTC format
  • statusobject: contains the campaign results for this specific record
    • omitted if the list is not assigned to the campaign or the campaign doesn't exist
    • field names are predefined
    • completed field is always present, while the other fields may be absent if the record was never called or never reached an agent.

item.description:
Bright Pattern's List Management API provides a convenient way to perform routine campaign management tasks without the Contact Center Administrator application. The API methods described in this section let managers duplicate, update, or delete campaigns; manage link groups; control campaign state; modify specific outbound dialing settings; configure caller ids, dispositions, and dial rules; and assign or remove lists.

Bright Pattern Contact Center solution defines several outbound campaign types - Outbound Voice, Blended Voice, and Outbound Messaging. Unless otherwise stated, the API methods described in this section and the following sections support all campaign types. If a method does not support Outbound Messaging (and applies only to Outbound Voice and Blended Voice), this is explicitly noted in that method’s description.

Note: Performing operations on all campaigns requires the user to have the "Manage all services and campaigns" privilege, configured in the Contact Center Administrator application. Alternatively, the "Manage assigned services and campaigns" privilege must be enabled for users to manipulate only their assigned campaigns. Additional privileges required are explicitly specified in the corresponding method descriptions.

The methods described below use the path variable, campaign_id, to reference the campaign, an operation is to be performed on. The unique identifier of a campaign can be found by opening that campaign in the Contact Center Administrator application, Services & Campaigns section. The id will be displayed in the '#SERVICES_CAMPAIGNS:SERVICES_PROPERTIES:' fragment of the URL.

Alternatively, campaign_id, can be found in the response body of the Get Campaigns method (see here).

item.description:
Bright Pattern's List Management API streamlines the creation and deletion of lists and formats and provides a convenient way to manage list records.

Note: Performing operations on lists requires the user to have the "Manage Lists" privilege, configured in the Contact Center Administrator application. Additional privileges required are explicitly specified in the corresponding method description.

All of the methods described below use the path variable, list_id, to specify the list an operation is to be performed on. The unique identifier of a list can be found by opening that list in the Contact Center Administrator application, Lists section. The id will be displayed in the '#LISTS:LISTS_PROPERTIES:' fragment of the URL.

Alternatively, list_id, can be found in the response body of the Get Lists method (see here).

Methods retained from the previous version of the List management API, tagged as "DEPRECIATED", require an additional path variable, campaign_id, to reference the campaign associated with the selected list. The unique identifier of a campaign can be found by opening that campaign in the Contact Center Administrator application, Services & Campaigns section. The id will be displayed in the '#SERVICES_CAMPAIGNS:SERVICES_PROPERTIES:' fragment of the URL.

Alternatively, campaign_id, can be found in the response body of the Get Campaigns method (see here).

Note: When importing records or updating records it is important to remember that:

  1. All leading and trailing whitespaces should be deleted.

  2. For all PHONE numbers:

    1. If a number begins with “+”, the leading "+" sign will be removed.

    2. If a number contains non-numeric characters, they will be removed.

    3. At least one PHONE number is required.

  3. For the United States and Canada PHONE numbers:

    1. If a number begins with “011”, it will be kept as is.

    2. If a number begins with “1” and has eleven digits, it will be kept as is.

    3. If a number does not begin with “1” and has ten digits, “1” will be prepended.

    4. If a number begins with “1” and has ten digits, the record will not be imported, returning a format error.

    5. In any other case, the record will not be imported, returning a format error.

    6. Remove prefix and Default country code fields will be ignored.

  4. For Other countries PHONE numbers:

    1. If a number begins with prefix matching Remove prefix, the prefix will be deleted.

    2. If a number does not begin with prefix matching Remove prefix, it will be kept as is.

    3. If a number does not begin with prefix matching Default country code, Default country code will be added.

  5. For all INTEGER fields:

    1. If the value is presented as a string, it should be converted to an integer.

    2. Values presented as integers should be supported.

  6. For all fields that expect strings (ACCOUNT, AGENT_LOGIN_ID, FIRST_NAME, LAST_NAME, etc.) integer values should be converted to strings.

  7. Capitalization matters: values with different capitalizations are treated as distinct.

  8. For all DATE/TIME and DATE/TIME - SCHEDULE CALL AT fields:

    1. If a value is not valid date/time, the record will not be imported with formatError.

  9. The search can be performed by both the original values created in third-party systems and their transformed equivalents visible in the Administrator Application and Agent Desktop.

item.description:
Bright Pattern's List Management API makes it easy to manage the contents of Do Not Call (DNC) lists with bulk delete, add, and replace actions. The API methods described in this section fully support Internal, Geographic (Postal), Geographic (Area codes), and Record Exclusion DNC list types. Geographic (State/Province) DNC List type is not supported in the current implementation.

Note: Performing operations on DNC lists requires the user to have the "Manage Lists" privilege, configured in the Contact Center Administrator application.

The functionality of the API methods described in this section is built upon a DNC List Record JSON Object with a required non-empty key field and an optional comment field. Depending on the DNC list type, the object's field values vary as follows:

DNC List Type Field Values
Internal key (required field): Phone number
comment (optional field): Campaign Name
Geographic (Postal) key (required field): Postal Code
comment (optional field): Notes
Geographic (Area Codes) key (required field): Area code
comment (optional field): Notes
Record Exclusion key (required field): Exclusion field
comment (optional field): -

Note: When importing records or updating records it is important to remember that:

  1. All leading and trailing whitespaces should be deleted.
  2. All integer values should be converted to strings.
  3. Capitalization matters: values with different capitalizations are treated as distinct.
  4. The search can be performed by both the original values created in third-party systems and their transformed equivalents visible in the Administrator Application and Agent Desktop.

item.name: Cursor-based Pagination
item.description:
Cursor-based Pagination, utilized in many of the Bright Pattern's List Management API methods is a current state-of-the-art approach to dealing with large volumes of data.

In cases where API requests are expected to contain many and many rows of records, returning them all at once is not an option. Instead, it makes sense to return one subset of a predefined size, a page, at a time. This technique, called paging, is commonly used across the majority of APIs. The cursor-based part of our approach comes from the idea of using a "cursor" - something like a bookmark that points exactly to where you left off.

At the core of Cursor-based pagination lies a rather basic concept of pointers. The pointer in this case is called a "cursor", and is used to reference a specific record in a database. In each request, clients pass cursor along with page_size parameter that specifies the number of records returned per page.

It is important to remember that:

  • The cursor must refer to a specific unique value in the database.
    • If the cursor value is not provided, the first record in the database will be used by default.
  • The number of records, specified in page_size , with corresponding field values less than the value of cursor are returned.
    • If the number of records returned is less than page_size, it implies that there are no more records and the page returned was the last one.
  • The record whose position is page_size + 1 is passed back to the client as the next_cursor.

item.name: Error Handling
item.description:
Note: This section provides general information regarding unsuccessful execution responses. We recommend you refer to the Response Codes description provided for each method individually for more specific information about any encountered errors.

Bright Pattern’s List Management API utilizes standard HTTP codes to indicate successful execution and flag errors if any occur. For each error listed in this documentation, the response includes the following information:

  1. Human-readable error name - e.g. "bad_request"

  2. Detailed description of what caused the error to occur - e.g. "'parameter_name' has unsupported value 'parameter_value': integer is expected"

and has the following format:

{ 
  “error”: “name”, //error name
  “error_description”: “description” //detailed description of the reasons that led to this error
}

Note: We highly recommend paying close attention to the content of error_description as it offers useful information to aid debugging.

Possible Errors

The table below contains the full list of HTTP errors and specifies possible underlying reasons for each of them.

Error Description Possible Reasons
400 Bad Request Request cannot be processed due to a format error - Empty or missed required parameter
- Duplicated parameter
- Unsupported parameter
- Wrong value format or value out of boundaries
401 Unauthorized Authentification failed for some reason - Wrong Client ID/Secret or Grant type
- Tenant is inactive
- Client is disabled or locked out
- Token is expired or has an invalid format
403 Forbidden Requested operation cannot be performed due to insufficient privileges on the current user's profile - User is authenticated but doesn't have sufficient privileges
404 Not Found Specified resource cannot be found - Wrong path or key
- Wrong or missing object ID
405 Method Not Allowed Requested method cannot be performed for the specified resource - Wrong request type
- HEAD request type
409 Conflict Request conflicts with the current state of the server - Duplicate or missing value
- Issue with specified instance
- Campaign is already in the requested state
- List is not bound to the specified campaign
415 Unsupported Media Type Media format of the requested data is not supported - No content type in HTTP header
- Content type is text/plain but JSON is expected
